text:
alice: Quick Q — we have a couple services (ingest-worker, router) that log their env on startup for debugging. Should we auto-redact env vars that look like secrets (API_KEY, *_TOKEN, PRIVATE_KEY) or rely on k8s secret handling? I noticed full values in logs for a couple deploys.

ben: We should definitely redact. Observability has a rule about not logging high-entropy values. Are these logs from our code or from a 3rd-party lib?

carol: Mostly our init code. Easy fix: add a small redaction step before any env dump. Example (Python):

```python
import re
SECRET_RE = re.compile(r'(?:key|token|secret|password)$', re.I)

def redact_env(env):
    out = {}
    for k, v in env.items():
        if SECRET_RE.search(k) or (isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > 40):
            out[k] = '<redacted>'
        else:
            out[k] = v
    return out
```

We can also flip on this only in prod via REDACT_ENV=true.

dave: Related note: if you're decrypting env at startup via KMS, and you want an HSM-backed signing key (for SSO or inter-service signing), importing key material into the HSM is possible but requires extra approvals. That import flow is different from generating a key in-cloud.

infra-bot: FYI — secrets policy link: https://redwood.internal/security/secrets-policy (see section 4.3 on KMS/HSM imports).

alice: @elaine quick ping — I'm planning a private-deploy for customer X and want to import an existing HSM key for token signing. Is that allowed and what approvals do I need to attach to the ticket?

elaine: Short answer: allowed with controls. Required items before import:
- JIRA ticket with business justification and key owners
- SCAB (Sec Change Advisory Board) sign-off
- KMS key policy and least-privilege IAM bindings
- Rotation frequency documented (max 12 months for signing keys unless justified)
- Threat model + list of principals that can use the key

Also: do not store private key material in plaintext anywhere; use secure staging for the import bundle and rotate access credentials immediately after import.

carol: Back to logs — propose adding a LogRedaction middleware in our common lib and a small fluentd rule to mask on ingestion. Example config snippet for the middleware toggle: 

```yaml
log_redaction:
  enabled: ${REDACT_ENV:false}
  patterns:
    - '.*_KEY$'
    - '.*TOKEN.*'
    - 'PASSWORD'
```

And add a one-line unit test to ensure values are replaced with <redacted>.

ben: Sounds good. I'll open an RFC and include the security checklist and fluentd masking suggestion. +1 on middleware. We should also scan historical logs for accidental exposures and rotate any leaked keys.

alice: I'll open INFRA-4321 with the HSM import request and attach the checklist + threat model. Will also schedule a quick 15m with @elaine if you want to triage before SCAB. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

elaine: Thanks — please CC sec-approvals mailbox on the ticket and include the principal list. We'll aim for a SCAB review in the next 3 business days.

ben: One more note — add a log hook to redact stack traces that include environment fragments (seen in a bug where an exception printed repr(os.environ)).

alice: Good catch, will add that to the ticket. Closing loop here.
